"a) a group data item that contains an occurs-depending table."
"b) an occurs-depending table."
"c) a data item that is subordinate to an occurs-depending table."

findings.why_it_matters: The list nesting is the only thing that binds a)/b)/c) and the closing paragraph to general rule 6) of 13.18.63.4. At column 0 they read as free-standing top-level items sitting between rule 6) and rule 7), so a reader (or a tool slicing rules by indentation) can attach them to the wrong rule or treat the closing sentence as a general statement about all VALUE clauses rather than a rule about occurs-depending tables. The transcription's own convention indents sub-items everywhere else in this very subclause -- line 23071 is "   c) for all other items" under rule 4), and the a)/b) of rule 16) on page 553 (lines 14 and 16 of the page-553 slice) are indented 3 spaces -- so this block is an isolated anomaly, not a house style.
